name: Foxglove
description: A single-file H5 e-reader with no pages in its data. A book is one long string; the pages are walked out of it on the spot from however many characters fit, which is the type size times a margin factor, and every break snaps back to the last space. Make the type bigger and the book gets longer — the same words, more pages. Your place, your bookmarks and your highlights are therefore kept as character offsets, so changing the type size moves a bookmark to a different page number and leaves it on exactly the same sentence. 6 screens, 4 books, 4 type sizes, 3 margin widths, 3 colour themes, full-text search.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

observation.text: engine.a11y(state) — the page text itself, the page number, the characters-per-page figure and the offset all serialise.
observation.pixels: 390x844 screenshot (browser backend); the type size and theme are real CSS, so the page looks like what it says it is
observation.state: engine.snapshot(state) — canonical state plus a derived view with offsets, page numbers and the quoted text at each mark. For the verifier only.

world.pagination: characters per page = type size figure x margin factor / 100; pages are walked from the start and each break moves back to the last space
world.position: kept as a character offset, never as a page number
world.marks: bookmarks and highlights are offsets too, so they survive re-pagination on the same words
world.counts: at Medium and Normal the main book is 4 pages; at Huge it is 8
